definition: Techniques for combining the weights of multiple trained models (often fine-tuned variants of the same base model) into a single model without additional training.
details: Model merging methods, such as weight averaging or task-vector arithmetic, can combine capabilities from multiple specialized fine-tunes into one model at little to no additional training cost.
story: Think of a hiker descending a foggy hill in the dark, taking small steps and feeling for the steepest way down. Boil it down and it is this: Techniques for combining the weights of multiple trained models (often fine-tuned variants of the same base model) into a single model without additional training. Here is why it matters: Model merging methods, such as weight averaging or task-vector arithmetic, can combine capabilities from multiple specialized fine-tunes into one model at little to no additional training cost. Skill, for a model, is just error pushed down until it is small enough to ignore. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Model Merging.
